name: Ruby Community Style Guide
description: Enforces Ruby community style conventions for readable, idiomatic Ruby code.
content:
# Ruby Community Style Guide Rules

- Use 2-space indentation, no tabs — this is the universal Ruby convention
- Prefer `snake_case` for methods and variables, `CamelCase` for classes and modules, `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE` for constants
- Use `do...end` for multi-line blocks and `{ }` for single-line blocks
- Prefer `unless` over `if !condition` for simple negations — but never use `unless` with `else`
- Use guard clauses (`return early`) to reduce nesting instead of deeply nested if-else
- Prefer string interpolation `"Hello #{name}"` over concatenation `"Hello " + name`
- Use `freeze` on string constants to prevent mutation — `MY_CONST = 'value'.freeze`
- Prefer `each` over `for` — `for` leaks variables into the surrounding scope
- Use `Symbol#to_proc` shorthand — `array.map(&:to_s)` instead of `array.map { |x| x.to_s }`
- Use `attr_reader`, `attr_writer`, `attr_accessor` instead of manually writing getters/setters
- Prefer `raise` over `fail` for exceptions — use `fail` only in rescue blocks for re-raising
- Run RuboCop in CI with a project `.rubocop.yml` — enforce style consistently across the team
